'''Xakriabá''' (also called '''Chakriaba''', '''Chikriaba''', '''Shacriaba''' or '''Shicriabá''')<ref>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190605214821/http://www.multitree.org/codes/xkr.html|url=http://www.multitree.org/codes/xkr.html|title=Shakriabá|url-status=dead|archive-date=5 June 2019|publisher=[[Linguist List|LINGUIST List]]|access-date=7 November 2024}}</ref> is a dormant [[Central Jê languages|Akuwẽ (Central Jê)]] language ([[Jê languages|Jê]], [[Macro-Jê languages|Macro-Jê]]) formerly spoken in [[Minas Gerais]], [[Brazil]] by the [[Xakriabá people]], who today speak [[Portuguese language|Portuguese]].<ref name="moseley-2007"/> The language is known through two short wordlists collected by [[Augustin Saint-Hilaire]] and [[Wilhelm Ludwig von Eschwege]].<ref name="Nikulin-Macro-Je">{{cite thesis|last=Nikulin |first=Andrey |date=2020 |url=http://etnolinguistica.wdfiles.com/local--files/tese%3Anikulin-2020/Nikulin_2020_Proto-Macro-Je.pdf |title=Proto-Macro-Jê: um estudo reconstrutivo |type=Ph.D. dissertation |location=Brasília |publisher=Universidade de Brasília}}</ref>{{rp|14}}<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Rodrigues |first=Ana Paula Santos |last2=Silva |first2=Manoel Antônio de Oliveira |date=2024-03-29 |title=Os cantos Xakriabá e a retomada da língua akwe᷉ |url=https://cadernos.abralin.org/index.php/cadernos/article/view/691 |journal=Cadernos de Linguística |volume=5 |issue=1 |pages=e691 |doi=10.25189/2675-4916.2024.v5.n1.id691 |issn=2675-4916}}</ref>

== History ==
Before 1712, Xakriabá was originally spoken along the [[São Francisco River]] near [[São Romão]], [[Minas Gerais]]<ref name="Ramirez">Ramirez, H., Vegini, V., & França, M. C. V. de. (2015). [https://periodicos.sbu.unicamp.br/ojs/index.php/liames/article/download/8642302/19659/ Koropó, puri, kamakã e outras línguas do Leste Brasileiro]. ''LIAMES: Línguas Indígenas Americanas'', 15(2), 223 - 277. {{doi|10.20396/liames.v15i2.8642302}}</ref> ([[Augustin Saint-Hilaire|Saint-Hilaire]] 2000: 340–341).<ref>Saint-Hilaire, Auguste de. 2000. ''Viagem pelas províncias do Rio de Janeiro e Minas Gerais''. Belo Horizonte: Editora Itatiaia.</ref> The Xakriabá were then forced to migrate after being defeated by {{ill|Matias Cardoso de Almeida|pt}} and other [[Bandeirantes|Paulistas]] from 1690 onwards. In 1819, Saint-Hilaire (1975: 145)<ref>Saint-Hilaire, Auguste de. 1975. ''Viagem à província de Goiás''. Belo Horizonte: Editora Itatiaia.</ref> noted that the Xakriabá of [[Triângulo Mineiro]] region spoke a [[Xerente language|Xerente]] dialect.<ref name="Ramirez" />
